subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@cloudfin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@cloudfin.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration and next steps

Thanks again for the demo this morning — good conversation. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying Qs so we’re aligned before the technical deep dive: 

Summary of pain points we discussed:
- High latency and CPU spikes on our inference tier during peak batch jobs (not consistent across request sizes).
- Current costs for embeddings + reranking are the single biggest line item for our search experience team.
- Need deterministic structured outputs for downstream billing systems (we can’t rely on free-form text).

What we need / goals:
1) Streaming + function calling to build an interactive UI that can call internal tools and return structured JSON (safely).
2) Embeddings + reranking at scale (weekly batch + per-query real-time rerank) with cost predictability.
3) Compatibility with our SDKs (Python/Node) and an easy migration path — minimal model-side changes if possible.

Questions:
- Can Redwood’s SDK support function calling-style structured outputs (JSON schemas) today, or is that a roadmap item?
- Do you have an example integration for streaming -> function call -> structured output?
- What quantization / instance types do you recommend for embeddings at our scale?

Attachments: call_recording_20260225.mp4 (meeting recording), procurement_questionnaire.pdf (our procurement team sent this).

Next steps suggested from our side: technical deep-dive with your solutions engineer, sandbox access to test streaming + rerank latency, and a ballpark purchase order for benchmarking.

—Alex Johnson
CTO, CloudFin
alex.johnson@cloudfin.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@cloudfin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration and next steps

Alex — really appreciate the clear recap. Great to hear we’re aligned on the main goals. I’ll summarize responses inline below and propose concrete next steps.

Inline answers / recap:
- SDK & function calling: Redwood’s SDKs (Python/Node) already support function calling and structured outputs. We expose a JSON schema enforcement mode so the model returns valid JSON, plus an SDK helper that validates and falls back to a sanitized structured response if a parse fails. We’ll share a minimal example repo.
- Streaming + function call pattern: yes — we support streaming tokens and a deterministic function-calling flow. Typical pattern is: stream tokens to the client, detect function call in the stream, call the function, then stream back the structured result. We have a sample that wires streaming -> function call -> structured JSON which we’ll attach as a short walk-through.
- Embeddings & reranking: we recommend our quantized embedding models for batch/rerank workloads. For real-time per-query rerank, we suggest a 4-GPU dedicated pool (or our Dedicated offering) with caching on the top-k prefixes to reduce per-token costs. We’ll include a cost/latency estimate based on your approximate qps.

Attachments: integration_plan_v1.pdf (high level integration approach + sandbox instructions).

Proposed next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive (solutions eng + infra) — 60–90 min: demo streaming + function call pattern on a sample app. (Rishi to own scheduling).
2) Sandbox access for CloudFin with sample dataset + test keys (expires in 30 days).
3) Short procurement touchpoint — Lauren will follow up on the questionnaire and provide a PO template / pricing options.

Can you confirm preferred time windows for the deep-dive next week? I’m available Tue/Wed afternoons PST.

Thanks — I’ll also include code snippets and the sample repo link in the next email.

—Marissa Cole
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@cloudfin.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 13:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration and next steps

Looping in Lauren to pick up procurement and PO/contract questions. Lauren — can you review the procurement_questionnaire.pdf that Alex attached and suggest next steps? I’ll schedule the tech deep-dive once Alex confirms times; Marissa, please share the sample repo and streaming+function-calling example when ready.

Quick note on pricing & deal motion: based on the described volume (embeddings + rerank heavy), we should propose: 1) a 3-month pilot (metered) with a discounted embedding bundle for batch, and 2) optional Dedicated capacity if CloudFin needs consistent latencies at scale. I’ll draft an initial quote and add the RF-2026-0823 id.

—Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that all looks good to us. Tue/Wed afternoons PST next week work. Priya and I reviewed the integration_plan_v1.pdf and the streaming/function-calling approach sounds promising. A few follow-ups from security/procurement:
